message.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en"><p>Building Energy Modeling (BEM) is moving from expert-operated software toward Large Language Model (LLM)-based agentic systems that decompose user requests into specialized agents and executable tool calls. The LLM backend becomes part of the energy-modeling infrastructure, shaping routing reliability, latency, provider cost, and the inference burden incurred before a simulation even runs. Yet model choice is rarely quantified for localized agentic BEM, particularly when different language instructions must preserve canonical tool names, blackboard state, file paths, and engineering parameters. This study evaluates seven LLM backends, including a small local model and several regional models, using a bilingual worker-routing benchmark of 100 manually checked tasks per language covering prototype generation, quantitative modification, object insertion, simulation, output retrieval, comparative analysis, state-aware model selection, and missing-information detection. The strongest regional models achieved Chinese perfect-success rates of 98-99%, comparable to 97% for the baseline. Cost and latency analysis show that accuracy alone is insufficient for deployment selection. DeepSeek-V4-Pro provided the strongest cost–accuracy trade-off in this benchmark, requiring about US $119 per million Chinese worker-routing tasks and US $122 per million successful tasks. The corresponding success-adjusted cost was about 3.6× higher for the overseas baseline, 4.6× higher for MiniMax, 17.5× higher for Kimi, and 21.2× higher for GLM. A relative EnergyIndex further shows that low single-call inference burden can mislead when success rates are low. These results demonstrate that localized LLM selection is an operational design variable for reliable, cost-effective agentic BEM, and motivate end-to-end validation on full OpenStudio/EnergyPlus workflows.</p></jats:p>
title: Localized LLM selection for agentic building energy modeling worker routing
